pages.title: Macrauchenia
pages.text: The Macrauchenia ($(o)Macrauchenia patachonica$()) is an extinct litoptern that lived in South America during the Pleistocene, disappearing at its end.$(br2)It had a long neck, long legs and three-toed feet, giving it a build somewhat like a camel. Its nasal opening sat high on the skull, between the eyes.$(br2)The first fossils were collected by Charles Darwin in Patagonia in 1834. Its closest living relatives are thought to be the odd-toed ungulates, such as horses and tapirs.
